Now the issue happens whet function tracing is enabled via the kernel

column2: as the weak records are enabled by the command line

column1: function tracing
The ftrace records have several accounting flags and a ref count. The
DISABLED flag is just one. If the record is enabled before it is marked
DISABLED it will get an ENABLED flag and also have its ref counter
incremented. After it is marked for DISABLED
the ref counter is cleared. There's sanity checks on the records that are
performed after an ftrace function is registered or unregistered
detected that there were records marked as ENABLED with ref counter that
should not have been.
Note
column2: the module loading code uses the DISABLED flag as well to keep its

column1: functions from being modified while its being loaded and some of these
flags may get set in this process. So changing the verification code to
ignore DISABLED records is a no go
column2: as it still needs to verify that the

column1: module records are working too.
Also
column2: the weak functions still are calling a trampoline. Even though they

column1: should never be called
column2: it is dangerous to leave these weak functions
